{"id":"project-LICHEN-worker6-9098.4","title":"test_multihop_latency_bounds.py: bound asserts tautological (poll at TX-start records ~0us)","description":"SECURITY false-confidence: almost every upper-bound assertion in python/tests/sim/test_multihop_latency_bounds.py is tautological. Metrics latency is `poll_time_us - tx_start_us` (metrics.py record_reception). These tests call get_rx_result immediately after start_transmission, then advance_to. In BARRIER_SYNC the medium delivers in-flight TX at t=TX-start, so recorded latency is 0us (or ~0).

0us always satisfies:
- HOP_LATENCY_BUDGET_US (300ms)
- MAX_P99_LATENCY_US (500ms)
- CATASTROPHIC_LATENCY_US (1s)
- chaos max_expected (350ms)

A real queueing spike, duty-cycle backoff, TDMA wait, or replay-window miss would never fail these tests because they do not measure airtime or end-to-end delay; they measure when the test decided to poll.

The file itself documents this in test_latency_consistent_across_hops (approx lines 251-256):
  \"Poll 1ms into airtime so latency is TX-start-to-RX, not 0us (polling at t=TX-start records min_us=0 and hides variance).\"
Sibling tests never apply that workaround:
- test_three_node_line_latency_bounded
- test_five_node_line_latency_bounded
- test_latency_under_concurrent_transmissions
- test_latency_bounded_with_added_delay
- test_latency_bounded_with_degraded_signal
- test_sustained_load_latency_bounded
- test_bursty_traffic_latency_bounded (ffrp only made the count/p99 asserts unconditional; samples are still 0us)

Compounding: test_latency_under_concurrent_transmissions asserts stats.count >= 1 then claims p99. With n=1, p99 == the single (likely 0us) sample. Congestion/DoS latency is not statistically observed.

Module docstring claims \"end-to-end delay remains bounded\" then notes the simulator only tracks per-hop TX-start-to-RX. Tests never accumulate hops, so a 5-hop path at 300ms/hop (1.5s E2E) still looks bounded. Replay windows, OSCORE/EDHOC timeouts, and TDMA (spec/02a-coordinated-capacity.md) care about elapsed time, not poll scheduling.

Security impact: green results currently certify latency SLAs under load/congestion/chaos that the tests cannot falsify. Operators could size replay windows, slot periods, or congestion response from vacuous evidence.

Fix: poll after a positive airtime offset (as the consistency test already does), or after TxEnd, so samples reflect delivery time not poll scheduling. Assert min_us > 0. Keep unconditional count/p99/max asserts. For congestion, require MIN_DELIVERIES_FOR_STATS not n>=1. If E2E is in scope, measure cumulative hop latency separately from per-hop samples.","acceptance_criteria":"- Bound tests poll after a positive airtime offset or TxEnd so recorded latency is not 0us by construction.
